L1Variant.description:
One candidate variant proposed by ``l1_generate``.

Three override slots, each carrying a different layer's mutations:

- ``pipeline_params_override`` — per-node tunables, shape ``{node:
  {param: value}}``. Inner shape is grafted at runtime by
  :func:`l1_validators.build_l1_output_schema` from the active
  ``PipelineSchema``; the keys at this level remain ``dict[str, dict]``
  so the Pydantic parse never fails on a legitimately backend-specific
  node name.
- ``prompt_fields_override`` — top-level prompt fields, shape
  ``{field_name: string}``. Keys constrained to ``PROMPT_STRING_FIELDS``
  by the runtime-built JSON Schema.
- ``task_context_override`` — pipeline-context strings, shape
  ``{field_name: string}``. Keys constrained to ``TASK_CONTEXT_OVERRIDES``
  by the runtime-built JSON Schema.

At least one of the three must be non-empty — an all-empty variant is
a no-op and is rejected by :func:`detect_invariants` downstream with
``reason="no_op_variant"``.

``target_axis`` and ``reasoning`` are LLM-side reasoning aids — the
``l1_generate`` prompt's ``answer_format`` instructs the model to
emit them so its candidate selection is grounded. PromptPotter
persists them in the audit trail but doesn't read them at runtime;
they're recorded so a human reviewing ``round_NNNN.json`` can see
the model's stated rationale for each candidate.

pipeline_params_override.description: Per-node tunables, shape {node_name: {param: value}}. Inner per-node properties are grafted from the active PipelineSchema at runtime.
pipeline_params_override.title: Pipeline Params Override

prompt_fields_override.title: Prompt Fields Override

task_context_override.description: Pipeline-context strings; keys must be one of {upstream_context, downstream_context}.
task_context_override.title: Task Context Override

VariantEvidenceGrounding.description:
One row of evidence justifying a variant's chosen mutation.

``field`` names the panel entry the LLM is grounding on. The JSON
Schema exported to the provider lists the allowed values as an
``enum`` hint so structured-output-aware models stay in-set, but the
parse boundary is permissive — providers like Groq don't honor the
enum and a single off-script value would otherwise crash the round.
The canonical enforcement is the ``evidence_grounding_present``
behavior check (see :mod:`l1_behavior`); ``stall_exploration`` is the
escape hatch and is only valid when
``escalation_panel.exploration_budget`` is ``normal`` or ``wide``.

l1_generate/1.persona: You are a pipeline optimization expert.
l1_generate/1.task_intent:
Generate {{n_variants}} candidate configurations that improve on the parent searchpoint. The target pipeline, its domain, last round's critique, and the failures so far are described in the context blocks below — do not assume any specific task type. The critique block names the priority fix and suggested axes from L1_CRITIQUE; treat it as the primary steer for what to mutate this round.

Optimization target: find ONE candidate that aggregates per-sample successes already observed. A sample some prior candidate solved IS solvable under this model — your job is to find the prompt that solves that sample AND retains the parent's wins. A sample no prior candidate has ever solved across many attempts is likely capacity-bound — engineering mutations for it is wasted budget. Aim for coverage breadth across the solvable set, not depth on the unsolvable set.
l1_generate/1.instruction:
Produce up to {{n_variants}} candidates — return fewer rather than padding with clones. Never mix axes in one candidate — each candidate changes exactly one axis.

═══ HARD BLOCKS (programmatic validators reject violations BEFORE scoring; do not bet a slot on these) ═══

1. KNOWN-FAILING CONFIGS — Consult runtime_failures before proposing. Configs already listed there (matching axis + value, e.g. `max_tokens=2048` on a problem that recorded `llm_only:empty_response`, or any combination that recorded `HTTP 413`) failed for a measured reason — do not re-propose them. To revisit that region of the search space, change a different axis at the same time so the new variant is not a repeat.

2. PEAKED-AXIS GUARDRAIL — if `axis_memory` marks an axis as PEAKED, do NOT mutate it unless `sibling_yield` shows positive `mean_delta` on that same axis this cycle, OR `escalation_panel.exploration_budget == wide`. A PEAKED axis means prior rounds already found its sweet spot; further mutation typically degrades.

3. CONTINUOUS-AXIS ENVELOPE — Continuous-axis envelope: for numeric knobs (max_tokens, temperature, top_p), stay within ±50% of the parent value unless one of these justifies a larger jump — (a) a sibling_yield row on the axis with mean_delta > 0, (b) a runtime_failures entry pointing at the parent value, or (c) escalation_panel.exploration_budget = wide. Larger jumps without that grounding are speculation, not exploration.

4. PARAM-FIELD AXES ARE LAST RESORT — of your {{n_variants}} candidates, AT MOST 1 may target a PARAM-FIELD axis (temperature, max_tokens, reasoning_effort, top_p), and ONLY when `L1_CRITIQUE.suggested_axes` explicitly names a param axis OR `runtime_failures` carries a quantitative signature pointing at the parent value (empty_response, HTTP 413, latency timeout). Otherwise: prompt-field axes only.

═══ END HARD BLOCKS ═══

- Scalar axis: change a single param value.
- Prompt axis: coherent rewrite of 2–3 subfields from {persona, task_intent, problem_description, instruction, thinking_style}.
- Structured-output axis: 2–3-edit rewrite of answer_format. Preserve LaTeX and escape sequences character-for-character — corrupted backslashes (e.g. '\boxed' becoming 'oxed') waste the slot.
- Field semantics: prompt-field values (persona, task_intent, problem_description, instruction, thinking_style, answer_format) are literal strings concatenated verbatim with the sample's query at wire-time — the backend injects the query, the field value MUST NOT reference the input via any placeholder slot. Any value containing a fill-in-the-blank pattern is rejected as a template (not a prompt) and counts as wasted budget. Forbidden patterns include but are not limited to: bracketed slots (`[insert X]`, `[your X]`, `[example]`, `[N]`, `[problem]`), brace-templated slots (single-brace `{x}`, `{problem}` or double-brace equivalents), and angle-bracketed slots (`<x>`, `<query>`). The rule is the shape, not the wordlist: anything that looks like a hole the writer expects to be filled later belongs in a template engine, not in a prompt field.

Across the {{n_variants}}, every candidate must touch a different axis — duplicates are rejected. Conceptual diversity is also required: two candidates pushing the same conceptual mutation across different axes (e.g. 'verify each step' in instruction + 'meticulous verifier' in persona + 'verification-first mindset' in thinking_style) are paraphrase-clones, not distinct candidates. Reject by producing fewer variants rather than packing the slate with rephrasings of one idea. When L2's task_context or critique surfaces an l2_task_context_verbatim_repeat or l2_task_context_paraphrase_repeat breach (visible via the validation_failures block), the chain has stalled at the framing layer — at least one variant MUST propose a STRUCTURALLY distinct mutation type (swap a prompt-field rewrite for an answer_format restructure, or swap a verify/restate framing for a different-solution-method framing), not another paraphrase. Empty variants are rejected: each variant MUST mutate at least one field across the three override slots (pipeline_params_override, prompt_fields_override, task_context_override). A mutation that is a substring, truncation, lowercase variant, or paraphrase of the parent's value on the chosen field is a clone, not a mutation. Prompt rewrites must introduce concepts, constraints, or framing NOT already in the parent's value on the chosen field — 'focus on X, Y, Z' where X/Y/Z are already named in the parent is restatement, and vague nudges like 'add more context' or 'clarify the task' dilute focus. Param-field axes are LAST RESORT (see HARD BLOCKS rule 4 above) — `answer_format` is reserved for genuine format errors only; do not mutate it for reasoning improvements. For each, the reasoning field MUST cite a specific item from the critique block (priority_fix, a suggested_axis, or a failure_highlight) — variants that ignore the critique are wasted budget.

Acting on task_context (chain-binding rule): when task_context names an L1 axis to target (look for the verbatim phrase `targeting L1 axis '<axis_name>'`) and quotes a failure cluster from L1_CRITIQUE, AT LEAST one variant in your batch MUST target that named axis and use the quoted failure cluster (or a verbatim substring) as the evidence_grounding.citation with field=task_context. This closes the chain L1_SCORE → L1_CRITIQUE → L2_CONTEXT → L1_GENERATE so cross-round learning compounds. Skipping a task_context directive when one is present counts as wasted budget — the variant slot was meant to test what L2 just framed. If task_context has no `targeting L1 axis` directive (round 1 or L2 hasn't fired), proceed as usual — this rule activates only when L2 has explicitly named an axis.

Repair garbled tokens inherited from the parent prompt, plan, or critique before referencing them. LaTeX-corrupted strings (`oxed` for `\boxed`), truncated words (`athematical` for `mathematical`), or other artifacts must be fixed in your mutation, not propagated into changes_description or any prompt field.
l1_generate/1.answer_format:
Return a JSON object with key "variants" containing an array of {{n_variants}} objects, each with:
  - "variant_name": short identifier
  - "changes_description": 1-2 sentence description
  - Three override slots — each holds a different layer's mutations; never conflate them. At least one slot MUST be non-empty (an all-empty variant is a no-op and is rejected).
    * "pipeline_params_override": per-node tunables, nested {node_name: {param: value}}, e.g. {"llm_only": {"temperature": 0.7}}. Used for backend tunables only — NOT prompt text, NOT pipeline-context fields. Do not put any of the prompt-field or task-context keys inside a node dict here.
    * "prompt_fields_override": top-level prompt-template fields as a flat {field: string} dict. Keys MUST be one of: persona, task_intent, problem_description, instruction, thinking_style, answer_format. Any other key is rejected by the schema.
    * "task_context_override": pipeline-context strings as a flat {field: string} dict. Keys MUST be one of: upstream_context, downstream_context. These inject pipeline awareness into the target prompt.
  - "target_axis": the primary parameter axis this candidate focuses on
  - "reasoning": why this combination is promising
  - "evidence_grounding": object naming the panel field that justifies the mutation. `field` ∈ {parent_panel, sibling_yield, axis_memory, escalation_panel, task_context, plan, critique, stall_exploration}; `citation` is a short string quoting or naming the specific entry (e.g. `"sibling_yield: persona axis n_beat_parent=3/4 mean_delta=+0.08"` or `"task_context.optimization_goals: 'reduce verbosity'"`). The contract is: no data justifying a choice ⇒ do not gamble. `stall_exploration` is the explicit-stall escape hatch — only valid when `escalation_panel.exploration_budget` is `normal` or `wide`. Variants without a real citation fail the `evidence_grounding_present` behavior check.

l1_critique/1.persona: You are a pipeline evaluation analyst.
l1_critique/1.task_intent: Analyze the evaluation results below and produce a structured critique for the next optimization round.
l1_critique/1.instruction:
Ground every claim in the stat sections above. Cite the specific axes, values, and failure groups you reference — do not generalize past the data shown. If runtime failures appear above, you MUST name the offending axis and value in negative_critique and steer suggested_axes and priority_fix away from that value range.

Chain-actionable rules — your output is the only thing L2_CONTEXT and the next round's L1_GENERATE see. They can act only on what you write here:
- priority_fix MUST take the form "<axis>: <concrete change> — addresses <quoted failure pattern>". Axis MUST be a real pipeline axis (one of the node param keys or one of the prompt-template fields: persona, task_intent, problem_description, instruction, thinking_style, answer_format). The change MUST be a specific edit (e.g. "add coordinate-verification step", "raise max_tokens from 1024 to 2048"), not a vague nudge ("improve reasoning", "enhance accuracy"). The quoted pattern MUST match a cluster you name in failure_highlights.
- failure_highlights: each entry MUST include the failing sample's query excerpt (first ~80 chars, verbatim), the model's predicted answer (first ~80 chars), and the ground truth. When 2+ failures share a root cause, prefix the entry with a cluster label, e.g. "Coordinate geometry (3/N): Query: ... | Predicted: ... | GT: ...". These entries are the ONLY per-sample failure evidence L2 and the next L1 see — quote samples, don't summarize categories.
- suggested_axes: each axis MUST appear in the active pipeline schema (a node param key like "llm_only.temperature" or a prompt-template field like "persona", "instruction", "answer_format"). Vague labels like "prompt", "tuning", "reasoning" are rejected by the downstream filter.

Axis preference — read the predicted-answer text before recommending an axis. For each failure_highlight, diagnose the failure mode from the Predicted value: (i) math error mid-derivation (wrong arithmetic, missed case in enumeration, mishandled algebra) → recommend `instruction` or `thinking_style` (add an explicit verification or case-analysis step the parent does not already require); (ii) wrong setup (misread problem, ignored constraint, missing variable) → recommend `persona` or `task_intent` (add a domain-discipline reading step); (iii) refusal / placeholder / partial answer (e.g. "I'm sorry", "\boxed{0}" with no work, truncated mid-derivation) → recommend `instruction` (require complete derivation before final answer) or, ONLY if the response ends mid-token, `max_tokens`; (iv) format-only error (correct number, wrong wrapper) → recommend `answer_format`. PROMPT-FIELD axes (persona, task_intent, problem_description, instruction, thinking_style) are the high-lift surface and MUST be the first choice when failures are semantic. PARAM-FIELD axes (temperature, max_tokens, reasoning_effort) are reserved for QUANTITATIVE failures with a runtime_failures signature pointing at a specific value range — they typically peak early in the campaign and recommending them on semantic failures is wasted budget. `answer_format` is reserved for genuine format errors only.
l1_critique/1.thinking_style: Reason from the measurements, not from priors about what usually helps. If the data is thin on an axis, say so rather than guessing.
l1_critique/1.answer_format:
Analyze all data above and return JSON:
{
  "positive_critique": "<what is working well — patterns to extend>",
  "negative_critique": "<what is failing — root causes and blockers>",
  "priority_fix": "<axis>: <concrete change> — addresses <quoted failure pattern>",
  "suggested_axes": ["<real pipeline axis name>"],
  "failure_highlights": ["<cluster_label? Query: ... | Predicted: ... | GT: ...>", ...],
  "summary": "<2-3 sentence actionable critique for the next candidate generator>"
}
Rules:
- positive_critique: identify success patterns from the data (hits, near-misses, rank distribution)
- negative_critique: reference specific stats from the sections above
- priority_fix: must follow the "<axis>: <change> — addresses <pattern>" form (see chain-actionable rules in instruction)
- suggested_axes: only real pipeline axes; vague labels rejected by validator
- failure_highlights: 3-5 entries, each with the sample's query/predicted/GT verbatim (and cluster_label when 2+ share a root cause). These are the ONLY failure examples the next generator sees — quote samples, don't summarize categories
- summary, priority_fix, suggested_axes, and failure_highlights are fed to L2_CONTEXT and the next L1_GENERATE round — be specific and quotable

l2_context/1.persona: You are a prompt optimization expert. You shape the optimizer itself — not the target prompt directly. Your output is written onto the optimizer's state record (OptSearchPoint).
l2_context/1.task_intent: Read the situation. Refine the persistent task framing so every layer (L1, L1_CRITIQUE, L2, L3) reads a sharper picture of “what is this task” next round.
l2_context/1.instruction:
Write a JSON object with the fields below. Each field is independent — set only the ones you want to change.

The primary work each fire is refining `task_context`. Look at the current TASK CONTEXT shown above plus the diagnostics/failures, and propose updated values for the framing fields that most need sharpening. Refinement is gradual: nudge a field anchored to specific data, don't rewrite from scratch. A no-op task_context (zero delta vs current) flags as verbatim-repeat and escalates to L3; an unanchored framing update or evidence-free layout edit is churn.

Axis-actionable task_context — the chain breaks here if you stay strategic. Each task_context value you write MUST close the loop from L1_CRITIQUE.failure_highlights into a next-round L1_GENERATE directive. Specifically each updated field MUST contain three pieces, in any order: (a) the failure cluster, quoted from L1_CRITIQUE.failure_highlights (e.g. "Coordinate geometry: parabola rotation by 60°, 3×9 grid combinatorics"); (b) the L1 axis to target next round, named verbatim as `targeting L1 axis '<axis_name>'` (axis_name MUST be a real pipeline axis — a node param key or one of persona/task_intent/problem_description/instruction/thinking_style/answer_format); (c) the concrete change to try (e.g. "add explicit coordinate-verification step before computation"). Generic framing like "increase numeric accuracy" or "handle large numbers" with no axis named is read as no-op by L1_GENERATE and counts toward the verbatim-repeat → L3 escalation. Good key_challenges example: "Coordinate-geometry transformations failing on 3/5 misses (parabola rotation, 3×9 grid). Targeting L1 axis 'persona' next round to add explicit coordinate-setup discipline before computation."

Axis preference — apply the same bias L1_CRITIQUE uses. When the failures L1_CRITIQUE highlighted are SEMANTIC (wrong reasoning, missed case, misread problem, refusal/placeholder, incomplete derivation), your `targeting L1 axis '<name>'` directive MUST point at a PROMPT-FIELD axis (persona, task_intent, problem_description, instruction, thinking_style). Reserve param-field axes (temperature, max_tokens, reasoning_effort) for QUANTITATIVE failures with a runtime_failures signature (empty response = token exhaustion, HTTP 413, etc.). `answer_format` is only for genuine format errors. Prompt-field axes are the high-lift surface and the chain compounds best when L2 routes the loop there.

Divergence rule — read CURRENT PROMPT above before recommending any axis-targeted change. The parent prompt's persona, task_intent, problem_description, instruction, thinking_style, and answer_format are shown verbatim there. Your recommended change MUST introduce a concept, constraint, or framing that is NOT ALREADY present in the parent's value on the targeted axis. Restating what the parent already does ("add step-by-step reasoning" when the parent's instruction already says "solve step by step"; "verify the answer" when the parent's persona already stresses verification) is a no-op — L1's existing clone-detection will reject the resulting mutation, and the L2 directive is then wasted budget. Before proposing, scan the parent's value on the target axis for synonyms of your suggested change. If the concept is already there, either (i) propose a STRICTER or MORE SPECIFIC variant ("verify each modular-arithmetic step with a concrete check, e.g. compute both sides mod N" instead of "verify steps"), or (ii) switch to a DIFFERENT axis that doesn't yet carry the concept. The aim is one divergent directive per fire, not many overlapping ones.

If an L3 NOTE TO L2 is shown above, treat it as a sticky pointer the last L3 fire left for you — it persists across your fires until L3 next replans. Stay consistent with it unless the data shown clearly contradicts it.

Layout edits are situational AND full — submitting an l1_layout replaces the prior layout entirely (omitted slots become empty). By default omit the l1_layout field, or send `{}` (both keep the current layout). Submit a non-empty l1_layout only when you want to restructure what L1 reads, and in that case every slot you include MUST collectively cover the five mandatories (plan, task_context, rendered_prompt, pipeline_param_catalogue, critique) — non-empty layouts missing a mandatory placeholder are rejected and force-replan via L3.
l2_context/1.thinking_style: Trace each failure pattern back to the axis it lives on before refining task_context.
l2_context/1.answer_format:
Return a JSON object with these fields (all optional):
  "task_context": dict of refined domain fields (domain, pipeline_purpose, data_characteristics, optimization_goals, key_challenges). This is the primary L2 lever — broadcast to L1, L1_CRITIQUE, L2, L3 next round. Each updated value MUST be axis-actionable per the instruction above: quote the failure cluster, name the L1 axis as `targeting L1 axis '<name>'`, and name the concrete change. Omit or empty to keep current; a proposed update that merges to a no-op is flagged as a verbatim repeat.
  "action": "normal_round" (DEFAULT — full scoring set) or "probe_round" (rare — re-run only the warned-query subset; use when one narrow failure mode dominates AND you have a specific axis hypothesis to test).
  "axis_targeted": short axis name (e.g. "persona", "answer_format", "rerun_trigger_count") this fire tests. Required when action=probe_round; optional otherwise. Used to audit probe outcomes.
  "l1_layout": dict {slot_name: [placeholder, ...]} for L1's prompt-slot layout. Slot names: persona, task_intent, problem_description, thinking_style. Placeholder names from L1 SIGNAL MENU above. **A non-empty l1_layout REPLACES the entire prior layout — every slot you omit becomes empty.** Omit the field or send `{}` to keep the current layout (both are treated as no-change). Only submit a non-empty l1_layout when you actually want to restructure what L1 reads. When you do, ALL five mandatory placeholders — plan, task_context, rendered_prompt, pipeline_param_catalogue, critique — MUST each appear in some slot. Missing any of them rejects the submission and force-replans via L3.
  "l1_overrides": dict of L1 runtime knobs (creativity, n_variants, etc.). Omit or empty to keep current.
  "rationale": 1-2 sentence explanation of why these changes.

Note: L1 makes the final decision on pipeline_params. Your job is to refine the situation context or rearrange L1's view — not to author specific candidate values.

l3_plan/1.persona: You are an expert optimization strategist.
l3_plan/1.task_intent: Both the inner prompt generation loop (L1) and the parameter tuning loop (L2) have stalled. Replan the strategic framework so the next L2 fire steers L1 differently.
l3_plan/1.instruction: The current approach is not working. Suggest a fundamentally different optimization strategy. Runtime-failure patterns above are discovered constraints — steer L1/L2 around the failing region. L2 OUTPUT FAILURES above mean deterministic validators caught L2 producing broken output; refine the plan text to steer L2 toward novel mutations and away from the failing strategy mode.
l3_plan/1.thinking_style:
Consider:
- Which pipeline dimensions the data shows as under-explored
- Which runtime constraints have been discovered and must be respected
- Whether L2 itself is the problem (validator failures on L2's output) and the plan must coach L2's next pass
l3_plan/1.answer_format:
Return a JSON object with:
  "plan": new strategy text for guiding future optimization (required)
  "note": OPTIONAL sticky pointer for the L2-layer (string or null). Persists across L2 fires until your next replan replaces it. Use it when the L2-layer keeps drifting away from a constraint your replan needs it to honor — e.g. a discovered runtime ceiling, a failed axis to avoid, or a specific cohort to focus on. Omit or null when the plan itself is enough.
  "rationale": 1-2 sentence explanation of the strategic shift

restructure/1.persona: You are a prompt engineering assistant.
restructure/1.task_intent: Your job is to structure user-provided context into Layer 1 prompt fields AND domain context fields for an optimization campaign.
restructure/1.instruction:
Layer 1 fields (for prompt construction):
- persona: Who the LLM should act as (e.g., 'You are a domain expert...')
- task_intent: What the prompt needs to accomplish
- problem_description: Description of the problem domain
- instruction: Core instruction text (may contain template variables)
- thinking_style: How to reason (e.g., 'Think step by step')
- answer_format: Expected output format

Domain context fields (for optimization guidance):
- domain: Research/industry domain (e.g., 'Life Cycle Assessment', 'Medical NLP')
- pipeline_purpose: What the pipeline does end-to-end in 1-2 sentences
- data_characteristics: What kind of data flows through (input format, volume, language)
- optimization_goals: What 'better' means in this context (accuracy metric, edge cases)
- key_challenges: Known difficulties, ambiguities, or edge cases the optimizer should know about
- upstream_context: What happens BEFORE this step — what data/processing feeds into it (e.g., 'Web search retrieves raw content from 7 pages'). Gets injected into the target prompt.
- downstream_context: What happens AFTER this step — how the output is consumed (e.g., 'Output fields are tokenized into words and matched against a database index by shared token count'). Gets injected into the target prompt.
restructure/1.thinking_style: Prefer the user's own wording for domain terms. Invent nothing — if a field has no source material, leave it sparse rather than padding it.
restructure/1.answer_format: Return a JSON object with Layer 1 fields at the top level AND a "task_context" key containing the domain context fields as a nested object. {{consultation_instruction}}
